topics.title: Background: the author and the Franco-Prussian War

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the historical setting of the story: France's defeat in the Franco-Prussian War and the passing of Alsace and Lorraine to Prussia.
Identify the author, the narrator and the point of view from which the story is told.

topics.title: Franz's morning: temptation, dread and the bulletin-board

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Franz's fear of a scolding and the temptations he resisted on his way to school.
Interpret the significance of the crowd at the town-hall bulletin-board and Wachter's remark.

topics.title: The unusual classroom: stillness, M. Hamel's dress and the village elders

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how the silence of the classroom and M. Hamel's special clothes signal a solemn occasion.
Explain why old Hauser and the other villagers sat on the back benches.

topics.title: The order from Berlin and M. Hamel's message on language

concepts.learning_objective: State the order from Berlin and its effect on the school.
Evaluate M. Hamel's view that everyone, including himself, was to blame for putting off learning.
Interpret M. Hamel's idea that holding fast to one's language is like holding the key to one's prison.

topics.title: The last lessons and M. Hamel's farewell

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the writing lesson, M. Hamel's last moments in the classroom and his farewell.
Interpret Franz's thought about the pigeons being made to sing in German.

topics.title: Working with words and noticing form

concepts.learning_objective: Infer the meanings of expressions such as 'thunderclap', 'in unison' and 'in plenty of time' from the context.
Recognise that English has borrowed words from many languages, as shown in the chapter's examples.
Identify the past perfect form in the story and explain its use to show an earlier past.
